q.t: The process by which plants make food using sunlight is…
q.e: Photo = light, synthesis = making. Plants make food using light energy.

q.t: The green pigment in leaves is…
q.e: Chlorophyll captures sunlight for photosynthesis.

q.t: Plants store food in the form of…
q.e: Glucose made in leaves is turned into starch for storage.

q.t: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
q.e: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen.

q.t: Which gas is released during photosynthesis?
q.e: Oxygen is given out as photosynthesis makes glucose.

q.t: Tiny pores on leaves are called…
q.e: Stomata let gases move in and out of the leaf.

q.t: Xylem carries…
q.e: Xylem carries water and minerals up from the roots.

q.t: Phloem carries…
q.e: Phloem carries food made in the leaves to other parts. (Ph for 'phood'.)

q.t: Which part of a plant is called its 'food factory'?
q.e: Leaves are broad, flat and green — built to catch light and make food.

q.t: Iodine turns blue-black in the presence of…
q.e: This test shows whether a leaf has made and stored starch.

q.t: In the three-pot experiment, which pot grows best?
o: The one with sunlight and water
q.e: Plants need both sunlight and water.

q.t: Why is a leaf boiled in alcohol before the iodine test?
q.e: Without decolouring, the green would hide the blue-black colour.

q.t: Why is the alcohol heated in a water bath, not over a flame?
q.e: Alcohol catches fire easily, so it must not be heated directly.

q.t: A variegated leaf (green + white patches) is tested. Which parts turn blue-black?
q.e: Only parts with chlorophyll make starch. This shows chlorophyll is needed.

q.t: A plant kept in the dark for 36 h gives no blue-black. What does this show?
q.e: No light → no photosynthesis → no starch.

q.t: Photosynthesis word equation:
q.e: Plants use CO₂ and water, with sunlight and chlorophyll, to make glucose and release oxygen.

q.t: Red ink in water rises into a white flower. Through which tissue?
q.e: Water and dissolved substances travel up through xylem.

q.t: Plants respire…
o: All the time, in all parts
q.e: Every living part of the plant respires day and night to release energy.

q.t: Plant respiration: glucose + oxygen → ?
q.e: Same as in animals: glucose is broken down using oxygen to release energy.

q.t: Stomata are mostly found on…
q.e: Most stomata are on the lower surface, seen by peeling a thin layer under a microscope.

q.t: Why is the plant destarched (kept in dark 2–3 days) before the CO₂ experiment?
o: So old stored starch doesn't give a false result
q.e: Any starch found afterwards must then be freshly made during the experiment.

q.t: In the CO₂ experiment, why is caustic soda put in the bottle?
q.e: The half-leaf inside gets no CO₂, so it can't make starch.

q.t: Gas collected from a water plant in sunlight makes a glowing matchstick flare up. The gas is…
q.e: Oxygen helps burning, so it makes the flame flare.

q.t: Germinating seeds in a sealed flask turn lime water milky. This shows they…
q.e: CO₂ turns lime water milky, so the seeds were respiring.

q.t: Why is the seed flask kept in the dark?
q.e: In light, photosynthesis would use up CO₂ and confuse the result. Darkness tests only respiration.

q.t: Some leaves are red but still make starch. Why?
o: They have chlorophyll hidden by other pigments
q.e: Other pigments mask the green, but chlorophyll is still there working.

q.t: Which direction does phloem carry food?
q.e: Food is made in the leaves and sent everywhere, including roots and seeds for storage.

q.t: Which is TRUE only of photosynthesis, not respiration?
q.e: Photosynthesis needs light and chlorophyll, and happens only in green parts.

q.t: In the three-pot experiment, why change only one thing per pot?
o: So any difference is due to that one thing
q.e: If two things change, you can't tell which caused the result.

q.t: Who studied how water, temperature and colour of light affect photosynthesis?
q.e: Rustom Hormusji Dastur, head of Botany at the Royal Institute of Science, Bombay.

q.t: In the CO₂ test, the half-leaf outside the bottle turns blue-black but the half inside doesn't. The conclusion:
o: Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis
q.e: Both halves had light, water and chlorophyll; only the inside half lacked CO₂, and it made no starch.

q.t: Photosynthesis and respiration in a plant: which statement is correct?
q.e: Photosynthesis makes glucose and releases O₂; respiration uses glucose and O₂ to release energy and CO₂.

q.t: A non-green root cell needs energy. Where does its food come from?
o: Phloem brings food from the leaves
q.e: Roots can't photosynthesise; phloem delivers food made in leaves.

q.t: Why are leaves broad and flat?
q.e: A larger surface catches more light for photosynthesis.

q.t: Which pot in the three-pot experiment may die?
q.e: Without water the plant can't make food or stay alive; it may die.

q.t: Stomata let in ___ during photosynthesis and let in ___ during respiration.
q.e: The gas exchange reverses between the two processes.

q.t: Glucose made by photosynthesis is useful because…
o: It is an instant energy source and can be stored as starch
q.e: Glucose gives quick energy; extra is converted to starch for storage.

q.t: A green stem also tests positive for starch. Why?
o: Green parts have chlorophyll and photosynthesise
q.e: Any green part with chlorophyll can make food.

q.t: If the stem of the red-ink twig is cut, the red colour is seen…
o: Inside the stem, in the xylem
q.e: The colour travels in the xylem tubes inside the stem.

q.t: Which is the best evidence that plants respire?
o: Germinating seeds turn lime water milky in the dark
Red ink rises in the stem
q.e: CO₂ given out in the dark (no photosynthesis) can only come from respiration.
